note: Full re-transcription from scratch; result differs substantially from the draft (A4:16 A4:16 D5:8 F#5:8^ x3, conf med), which appears to have assumed the wrong key signature (2 sharps) and wrong octave register. (2) Only TWO written groups/repetitions are printed in this crop (not three, despite the 'Whip-poor-will x3' lyric) -- each group is a dotted-eighth + two 16ths (beamed) + eighth, followed by an eighth rest, ending on a final barline. (3) Notated (pre-8va) pitches per group are G5(dotted 8th) Eb5(16th) G5(16th) Bb5(8th, sits on a ledger line above the staff -- this ledger line was initially mistaken for a fermata/flag in early passes but is definitively a ledger line for the A5 line beneath the B5 space), confirmed via heads.py step data cross-checked against pixel y-positions and staff-line spacing. Sounding (8va, +1 octave) = G6/Eb6/G6/Bb6, outlining an Eb-major triad shape (G-Bb-Eb), which is musically coherent with the 2-flat key signature. No fermata is actually visible anywhere in this crop -- the draft's '^' on the last note appears to have been invented; dropped it. Verified with tools/parsecheck.py -- OK.

Full re-transcription from scratch of all 9 crops (figs_new/p092_s00 through s08), superseding the draft (Bb4:16 Bb4:16 Eb5:8 G5:8 F5:16 r:16 x3, conf low), which does not match any of the 9 systems actually printed on the page -- treated as an unreliable guess and discarded. Each system prints a short 4-note-plus-rest cell (eighth, two beamed 16ths, accented eighth [accent '>' marks not encodable in this format, omitted], eighth rest) repeated 3x, matching the 'Whip-poor-will (cluck)' lyric printed under s00-s05 (lyric not repeated under s06-s08 but the musical cell is identical in form). Distinct melodic variants across systems: s00 Eb-C-Eb-G, s01/s02 G-Eb-G-Bb, s03/s04 Eb-Eb-G-Bb, s05 G-G-Bb-Bb (all in written Eb-major pitches, key sig applied). s06 is a stepwise D5-Eb5 variant ending G5 on reps 1-3 but F5(natural) on rep 4, and (like s07/s08) omits the trailing rest after its final repetition, ending straight at the barline. s07 and s08 are the only systems with an explicit '8va.' marking printed above the staff (verified visually) -- sounding pitch = written +1 octave; s07 is in Eb major (Ab-Eb-Ab-Eb pattern), s08 switches to a 2-sharp (D major) key signature for a wide-leap variant (D5-F#6 sounding, i.e. written D4-F#5) that was the hardest passage to verify: the heads.py detector threw multiple conflicting false-positive candidates (F4/A4/D5/F5 all fired near the same beam) because its elliptical matcher partially triggers on the thick sloped 16th-note beam itself, a known failure mode. I cross-checked by measuring per-row dark-pixel-density centroids against the calibrated staff-line y-positions (confirmed the method against the following note, which centered exactly on the D5 line as expected) and am reasonably confident in D4-to-F#5(written) for that beamed pair, but it remains the single lowest-confidence element in this transcription -- worth a second look against a higher-resolution source scan if available. All key-signature accidentals (Bb/Eb/Ab for Eb major; F#/C# for D major on s08) applied to the detector's bare letter-pitches. Full concatenated string verified with tools/parsecheck.py -- OK.

minor-scale strain (figs_new/p094_s00.png). No key signature at the clef (0 sharps/flats) -> A minor. The G#5->G-natural pair is a textbook melodic-minor raised-leading-tone/natural-descent, which is strong internal confirmation of A minor and of the pitch reading.

Confirms catalog audit SURPRISE: page 75 actually shows 4 distinct melodic variations, not 3 as the old note said. Crop p097_s00 contains TWO variations (var 1 ends at internal double-bar ~mid-crop, var 2 begins right after with new clef/key sig and a chromatic F#5 passing tone); p097_s01 = variation 3; p097_s02 = variation 4 (opens with a grace note A4 slurred into F5, plus an accent mark, both not encodable in this format so noted here). Var 1 pitches/rhythm are solidly cross-checked (near-high conf); var 2 has an unencoded staccato-looking dot near the peak note each repeat and an odd rest glyph (encoded r:8, Cheney's hook-shaped rest); var 3 and especially var 4's back half have some residual pitch/beam-grouping judgment calls in dense passages (detector threw spurious duplicate hits near sloped beams throughout, filtered by cross-checking zoomed crops, but a few notes in var 4 could not be triple-verified) — hence overall 'med' rather than 'high'. 8va not applicable (already at written pitch). Key Eb major (3 flats) confirmed from key signature in all 3 crops.

Confirms catalog audit: page 76 'Loud and rapid' Rose-breasted Grosbeak figure spans 3 systems (p098_s00, s01, s02), concatenated here in reading order. All three systems use the same running 16-16-8 (triplet-shaped double-beam group) / single-beamed-8th-pair rhythmic motif, built from a narrow C5-G5 stepwise range with recurring Cheney hook-shaped rests (encoded r:8) and a few accent marks (>) not representable in this encoding (noted, not encoded). Notably the melody stays diatonic (C/D/E/F/G/B, occasional B4) and never uses the key's flatted degrees (Bb/Eb/Ab) in this passage — worth flagging since it's what let me confirm rgro-draft (see that entry) is NOT a match for this content. Detector threw a number of spurious duplicate-pitch hits right next to real notes on sloped beams (classic false positive per METHOD.md); each was checked against a zoomed crop and dropped when no second notehead was visible. 'Med' confidence: pitches are solidly cross-checked against zoomed crops, but exact beam-grouping (which pairs are 16th vs 8th) involved some judgment in a few spots, particularly at low contrast beam junctions.

No pitch, rhythm only, rit. & dim. Staffless monotone row (figs_new/p102_s00b.png): 17 note-glyphs on a single line with no staff, marked 'f' at the start and 'Rit. & dim.' partway through. Careful pixel-level comparison of the note glyphs shows the first 11 have a double flag (16th notes, tight/even spacing ~50px) and the remaining 6 switch to a single flag (8th notes, wider spacing ~62px) with a small staccato dot added above each - i.e. the ritardando is written out as literally longer note values plus wider spacing, and the diminuendo as staccato dots, rather than any gradual/continuous ramp. Staccato dots on the second half are not representable in the pitch:dur format and are only noted here.
